recentItems.title: Connecticut News Today: Flooding swamps Bridgeport as police probe shooting, hit-and-run
recentItems.description:
Heavy rain and flooding caused major problems across Connecticut, particularly in Bridgeport where police responded to about 100 flood-related calls in five hours and residents reported streets covered in water. Flooding also impacted businesses in Westport and roads in Norwalk, while federal officials surveyed damage and discussed disaster assistance options. Other major stories include a drive-by shooting at a Bridgeport birthday party that left a man critically injured, new arrests in the hit-and-run death of Zandrea Harris, a rollover crash in Weston, and a successful boat rescue near Seaside Park.

recentItems.title: Hudson Valley News Today: Could more flooding be ahead after weekend storm damage?
recentItems.description:
Heavy rain and flash flooding caused significant problems across Westchester, prompting water rescues in Rye and Port Chester, road closures near I-95, and storm damage in Yonkers where a fallen tree crushed vehicles and brought down wires. Officials say impacted roads in Rye have reopened, while investigators continue examining a devastating house fire in New City. Other developments include the arrest of a man accused of robbing a bank in Nanuet, preparations for a gun violence prevention conference in Westchester, renewal of the school resource officer program in the Lakeland School District, and a United Way benefit honoring community leader Joe McCoy.

recentItems.title: Brooklyn News Today: Fatal playground shooting, flood risks and major investigations
recentItems.description:
Another round of heavy rain renewed flooding concerns across Brooklyn, with residents and business owners in Bushwick, Bed-Stuy and Canarsie describing repeated damage and dangerous conditions. Meanwhile, community members are mourning the deaths of 33-year-old Deon Miller and 35-year-old Antoine Utsey, who were fatally shot at Howard Playground. Other developments include the expected sentencing of Gary Anderson in a manslaughter case tied to a 2017 assault, a shooting in East Flatbush, a semi-truck fire in Bay Ridge, and several ongoing NYPD investigations involving robbery, theft and public safety incidents.

recentItems.title: Bronx News Today: Harlem vigil, deadly Hunts Point shooting and disease investigation
recentItems.description:
A family gathered for a vigil honoring 27-year-old Lovay Williams after police charged her boyfriend, 41-year-old Tiliek Thompson, with murder, strangulation, assault, child abandonment and other offenses in connection with her death. In Hunts Point, 29-year-old Luis Cano died after being shot on Lafayette Avenue, while other Bronx investigations include an 18-year-old shot in Tremont, a fire in Unionport and a reported assault involving a 4-year-old child at Joyce Kilmer Park. Officials also provided new details on a Legionnaires’ disease outbreak, confirming nine cases and identifying Yankee Stadium and Lincoln Hospital among locations that tested positive for the bacteria.

recentItems.title: 3 trains, 2 kids, $60 a day: The real toll of a New Jersey commute
recentItems.description:
For Brian and Molly of Rahway, New Jersey, getting to work in Manhattan requires three trains, careful planning and constant coordination. Between daycare and school drop-offs, train connections, pickup deadlines and a shared car, the couple says their daily commute can cost about $60 a day and creates ongoing stress when delays threaten their ability to get home on time for their children.

recentItems.title: Newark Airport’s new hack lets travelers skip the food line entirely
recentItems.description:
A new pilot program at Newark Liberty International Airport's Terminal C is allowing travelers to preorder food, snacks, medicine, and other essentials before reaching their gate. Flyers receive a notification on their phone and can place an order that will be waiting at a designated pickup shelf near the gate. United and OTG say the program is designed to save time and reduce stress for travelers on the go.

recentItems.title: A mother and baby’s murders remain a mystery 30 years later
recentItems.description:
Thirty years after the murders of 18-year-old Rhonda Johnson and her six-month-old son, Co'Ran, investigators are still searching for answers. Rhonda disappeared on her way to work in September 1996 and was later found shot to death in her car, along with her infant son. Detectives say advances in forensic technology could help solve the case, and a $50,000 reward remains available for information leading to an arrest.

recentItems.title: Bill Clinton, NY leaders honor Rep. Nita Lowey at emotional dedication ceremony
recentItems.description:
Former President Bill Clinton, elected officials, family members and community leaders gathered in Westchester to honor the legacy of former Congresswoman Nita Lowey. Lowey, who served the Hudson Valley for more than 30 years, is remembered as a trailblazer, mentor and champion for her constituents.

recentItems.title: 9/11 ground zero volunteer surprised with $45K backyard putting green
recentItems.description:
A retired FDNY firefighter who volunteered at Ground Zero on 9/11 received a life-changing surprise at his New Windsor home. Through a partnership between Celebrity Greens and Folds of Honor, Vincent Damato’s empty backyard was transformed into a custom $45,000 putting green. The gift honors a lifetime of service that included the Marines, New York State Police, and 23 years with the FDNY.
